Gelati Monastery

The monastery and academy founded by David the Builder, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Time needed
2 h
From Tbilisi
240 km · 3:30
Road
Paved
Car needed
Economy class
Season
All year
Entry
free

Gelati stands on a hillside eleven kilometres from Kutaisi and counts as the principal cultural centre of medieval Georgia. The monastery was founded in 1106 by David IV the Builder, the king who united the country and drove out the Seljuks. For him it was never only a religious house: an academy was established here teaching philosophy, geometry, rhetoric and astronomy, and contemporaries called it a second Jerusalem and a new Athens.

Gelati is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, and that status remains current.

The heart of the complex is the main Church of the Virgin. In the apse is a 12th-century mosaic of the Theotokos flanked by archangels — one of the largest surviving medieval mosaics in the Caucasus. The walls carry layers of fresco painted between the 12th and 18th centuries, including portraits of Georgian kings.

What you see on site:

  • the Church of the Virgin with its mosaic and multi-layered wall painting
  • the churches of St George and St Nicholas
  • the academy building, where the stone benches still stand
  • the bell tower and the spring beneath it

David the Builder's grave lies at the southern gate. By tradition the king asked to be buried in the entrance itself, so that everyone entering would step over him — a last, deliberately humble gesture from Georgia's most powerful medieval ruler.

Practical advice

This is an active monastery: women need a headscarf and long skirt, men long trousers. Wraps are usually available at the gate, but bringing your own is safer. Morning or late afternoon is better for the mosaic, when sunlight reaches the apse. The churches hold deep shade and stay cool, so a jacket is useful even in summer. Park at the lot by the gate. A cafe and toilets sit at the entrance; the nearest ATM is in Kutaisi.

How to get there from Tbilisi

From Tbilisi take the E60 past Gori and Khashuri and through the new Rikoti tunnels to Kutaisi — 230 km, about three hours twenty. From Kutaisi head northeast and cover the last eleven kilometres to Gelati. The whole route is paved, with the final section narrow but in good condition. An economy car is entirely sufficient. Fuel and ATMs are plentiful in Kutaisi. Motsameta Monastery sits on the same road, so combining both in one outing takes almost no extra driving.
